question: Explain the requirement under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 for a chartered accountant in practice to communicate with the previous auditor before accepting an audit, and discuss when failure to do so amounts to professional misconduct.
references: Clause (8) of Part I of the First Schedule
sources: The Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, section 22 and First Schedule, Part I

points.label: The provision
points.description: A chartered accountant in practice is guilty of professional misconduct if he accepts a position as auditor previously held by another chartered accountant without first communicating with him in writing.
points.basis: Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, First Schedule, Part I, Clause (8), read with section 22

points.label: Purpose of the communication
points.description: It lets the incoming auditor find out whether there are professional or other reasons not to accept the appointment, protects the outgoing auditor's interests, and guards against a client changing auditors to avoid an unfavourable report.
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics, guidance on Clause (8)

points.label: Mode of communication
points.description: The communication must be in writing and sent in a way that gives proof of delivery, such as registered post with acknowledgement or hand delivery against a signed receipt; merely posting a letter without proof of delivery is not enough.
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics, guidance on the mode of communication under Clause (8)

points.label: Audits covered
points.description: The requirement applies to all kinds of audit, such as statutory audit, tax audit, internal audit and concurrent audit, and not only to company audits.
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics, guidance on the scope of Clause (8)

points.label: Effect of the reply and related check
points.description: The duty is to communicate, not to get the previous auditor's consent; if no reply comes within a reasonable time the incoming auditor may accept, but must consider any reply received. For a company audit the auditor must also check that the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 on appointment and removal of auditors have been complied with.
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics on Clause (8); Chartered Accountants Act, 1949, First Schedule, Part I, Clause (9)
